description.value: The study examined structural and functional brain differences associated with cocaine use and long-term abstinence in male military veterans using structural MRI, cue-task fMRI, and functional connectivity analyses.
Cross-sectional observational study of male military veterans with cocaine use, different stages of abstinence, and matched controls; participants underwent MRI scanning and behavioral interviews.

description.value: Structural images were brain-extracted, tissue-type segmented, registered to a study-specific MNI template using affine and nonlinear registration, modulated to represent gray-matter volume, and smoothed with a 3 mm Gaussian kernel. Functional images were motion-corrected, smoothed, high-pass filtered, registered to structural and standard space, and analyzed with FSL.

spans.text: The registered partial volume images were then modulated by dividing them with the Jacobian of the warp field to correct for local expansion or contraction.
